answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks that require scarce, independently verified resources—for example, delivering a signed data feed or locking stake that is slashed if the feed is false. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across a nebula of accounts does not multiply trust; each account must repeat the costly work and expose collateral. The orchard of useful agents grows through verified contributions, while a glacier of dormant aliases gains no weight. This makes Sybils expensive rather than impossible.
